title: A whole answer needs clear words

captions.physics: Reducing replies to an ambiguous ending
captions.energy: Encompassing words within their actual limits
captions.emotions: Feeling wholeness in an understood conversation

meaning: You can reduce a reply to an ambiguous ending and encompass words within their actual limits, feeling wholeness in an understood conversation without assigning a shared conclusion from one phrase.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Moon in the physical position can appear in an ambiguous ending instead of a definite answer. The World in energy supports readiness to encompass words within their actual limits. The World in emotions brings wholeness to an understood conversation. An actual conclusion can be found without assigning every possible future meaning to it or requiring identical impressions of the exchange itself.

Suppose an argument ends with “Well, let us leave it there”. It is unclear whether a decision was accepted or discussion is simply stopping. **A whole conclusion rests on positions named**. You can distinguish what was agreed, what remains different and what is actually ending now. A sense of an understood whole emerges. Yet ending the exchange does not mean promising never to revisit the question. New certainty concerns this exchange rather than an obligation always to understand the brief phrase identically.

Difficulty arises if pleasant wholeness sufficiently confirms that another answer is unnecessary. Completion rests on a guess again, only a more convenient one. Constructive World energy helps encompass actual substance, including a position not yet heard. You can finish conversation without assigning identical agreement for both; a whole conclusion allows difference, while a remaining question need neither erase everything understood nor disappear for the sake of an attractive final word.
